title: Customer eval signal corruption caused by stop-pattern compatibility layer interacting with prefix caching
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Severity: Customers observed sudden spikes in eval failure rates and over-generation after the 1.20 compatibility change that normalizes legacy stop patterns. The issue is customer-specific and most visible for multi-turn eval suites that include short termination markers (e.g., '###', '
--END--').

Symptom: For affected customers (notably Acme Health and Veridian Labs), golden eval prompts that previously terminated cleanly now produce trailing tokens or entirely different termination points. The behavior is inconsistent across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private pools: Hosted manifests more often for short-sequence evals; Private pools show it when KV-prefix dedup is enabled.

Hypothesis: The compatibility layer introduced an internal canonicalization step that rewrites stop patterns to regex-like tokens and sets a flag on the request. When requests pass through prefix/KV cache merging in the routing layer, the merged metadata loses the original stop-pattern list in some codepaths, causing the runtime to fall back to a default 'no-stop' policy and produce over-generation. This only affects customers with mixed legacy stop pattern formats and who exercise prefix cache dedup (multi-turn evals or cached system prompts).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use customer prompt set with short stop markers (e.g. '###' and '
--END--') used across multi-turn evals.
2) Enable prefix/KV caching and run on a private pool that has prefix_dedup=true.
3) Call the API using a legacy SDK client that triggers the stop-pattern compatibility conversion header.
4) Observe generated outputs: termination occurs late or not at all, trailing tokens appended to JSON outputs or function calls not closed properly.
investigation_notes: 2025-02-18 10:12 - Initial report from Support (Priya Rao) after Acme Health flagged 18% regression on their eval pass rate.
2025-02-18 11:05 - Reproduced in-house using Acme test harness with prefix_dedup enabled (Ethan Brooks).
2025-02-19 09:34 - Kernel/runtime team confirmed that when stop list is missing, the sampling loop uses 'max_tokens' only and never enforces early-stop (Johan Müller).
2025-02-19 14:20 - Routing team found that metadata merging code in private routing overlay drops 'stop_patterns_v2' when route has 'compat_header' present (Liam Chen).
2025-02-20 16:02 - Confirmed Hosted path also suffers when request is routed through shared prefix cache in the edge layer; difference: fallback frequency lower due to different cache codepath.
root_cause: A two-part interaction: (1) compatibility normalization converts various stop formats into an internal canonical field and sets a compatibility header; (2) prefix/KV cache merging code in routing overlay did not include the canonical stop field in its merge set, causing some merged requests to lack stop metadata and fall back to default sampling behavior. The bug only surfaced after rollout of the compatibility layer and the prefix-dedup optimization were both live in production.
fix_summary: A. Patch routing overlay to include canonical stop metadata in all cache/merge operations (atomic metadata merge).
B. Introduce an integrity check asserting presence of stop metadata for requests that originate from legacy-compat clients (fails fast rather than silent fallback).
C. Add a targeted migration to keep original stop-patterns in a 'stop_patterns_raw' field preserved through merge to support later debugging and audits.
D. Add unit / integration tests that simulate prefix merge with various compatibility header combinations across Hosted/Dedicated/Private path.
rollout_plan: 1) Patch deployed to staging and private-canary pools (2025-02-24).
2) Run customer-specific regression harness for Acme and Veridian (overnight smoke).
3) Gradual rollout to Hosted edge (canary 5% 1 hour, 25% 4 hours) with realtime gauging on eval pass-rate dashboard.
4) Dedicated pool update scheduled with ops during quiet hours (2025-02-27 02:00 UTC).
5) Full rollback plan: revert routing overlay commit and toggle compat normalization via runtime feature flag.
test_plan: - Unit tests for metadata merge including stop_patterns_v2 and stop_patterns_raw.
- Integration test that runs 10k eval prompts from customer harnesses and asserts no change in termination distribution beyond 0.5%.
- Chaos test: simulate partial metadata loss and verify fail-fast assert triggers alert rather than silent over-generation.
- Add new golden test for SDK compatibility header + prefix cache scenario.
monitoring_and_metrics: Alarms: PagerDuty if eval_pass_rate drop >5% relative to baseline for any customer for 15m.
Post-deploy: track 24h rolling delta for Acme Health and Veridian Labs.

2) Audit other metadata fields that may be dropped during merge to prevent future regressions (scheduled Cycle 2025-W10).
3) Update SDK docs to recommend explicit 'stop' parameter until compat header is deprecated.
4) Postmortem write-up and shareable summary for Sales/CS with timeline and impact metrics.
